Independent first-plus/last-minus count and rational inequality rederived analytically
correctness.rationale: Free amalgamation over a common induced subgraph cannot introduce a cyclic triangle spanning the two new parts, since that triangle would need a cross-edge. Universality and homogeneity of this specified Fraïssé limit identify finite injective named extensions with the counted types. A unary sign word has no plus before a minus (otherwise x→v_i→v_j→x). Splitting on its last minus gives 2^n+n·2^(n−1); two valid words give any nonedge extension. For x→y the only extra forbidden simultaneous sign is (minus,plus). As an independent count, if y has no plus there are 2^n u_n pairs. If its first plus is at t, the cases where x has no minus or its last minus is before t give (t+1)4^(n−1); last minus at t is impossible. For last minus j>t the contribution is 4^(t−1+n−j)3^(j−t−1). Summing this last contribution over t<j gives sum_{d=1}^{n−1}(n−d)4^(n−d−1)3^(d−1)=(n−4)4^(n−1)+3^n (finite geometric sum, or its first difference). The total is the claimed a_n; at n=0 all three channels have one type. Exchanging the ordered coordinates reverses the arc channel. Cross-multiplying b_{n+1}/a_{n+1}>b_n/a_n yields the displayed sign expression in RESULT.md; its values at n=0,1,2,3 are 4,35/4,65/4,1735/64, and the polynomial term alone is positive for n≥4. Thus p_n strictly decreases; expanding numerator minus half the denominator gives the claimed 5/(4n) correction and limit 1/2.
residual_risks: The count uses ordered distinct fresh vertices over an individually named transitive complete base, not automorphism classes with base names forgotten or a sampling law on vertices.
